- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at 1–2% above true peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates 30d horizon; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon if sentiment >0.6.
- If model forecast dips below 55% of recent 18-day average, and sentiment is neutral or negative, add 1–2% upward bias to avoid prolonged underestimation.
- When sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.7 → 0.1 → 0.7), model often fails to anticipate mean reversion; apply 3–5 day lag correction: forecast = true outcome - 0.5×(forecast - true) for next 3 days.
- For 30d horizon, if model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
